newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr/mark retrenches, sets sights higher.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr/mark retrenches, sets sights higher.

text.p: Dollar/mark's retreat from a fresh 34-month high on Tuesday shook out excess long positions and should provide an initial base for further short-term highs in the rate, chartists said.
"We came in today, everyone was sitting around long and there was no one left to buy on a short-term basis," said Ture Johnson, technical analyst at Bank of America.
"This is the first natural cleaning out we've had in a while, so I think it goes down and lasts a day or so but then I think you form a base and go higher again," he added.
The dollar popped up to its highest level against the mark since April of 1994 in European trade on Tuesday, touching the 1.7050 threshold before sinking substantially during the U.S. session.
Technicians said Tuesday's high now represents the rate's next hurdle and said a break of that level would likely send dollar/mark rapidly higher.

"At the moment the outlook is still rather positive," said Ben Morden, technical analyst at I.D.E.A. Inc, citing an earlier break of a six-year downward tilting trendline at 1.6830 as reason for optimism.
"If you're a medium-term trader I think you have to look to the February 1994 high," Morden added. The high for February of 1994 comes in at 1.7686.
Chartists pegged key support in dollar/mark at 1.6750 and recommended buying the rate on any approach of that level.
The dollar was trading near its session lows at 1.6835/45 marks in the mid-afternoon on Tuesday.
"I think you start buying dollars ahead of 1.6750," said Bank of America's Johnson. "And even if it gets below that, somewhere soon you're going to have to buy it again."
